# FDG3068

> DO name collection properties with a plural phrase describing the items in the collection instead of using a singular phrase followed by “List” or “Collection.”

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 3.6.2 Names of Properties.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG3068
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Name the collection property '{0}' with a plural phrase instead of a 'List' or 'Collection' suffix

FDG3068 reports an externally visible property of an array or IEnumerable type (other than string) whose last word is 'List' or 'Collection', as in the book's bad example. It cannot tell whether the rest of the name is a plural phrase. Overrides and interface implementations are not reported. Known limitation: a compound noun that ends in the word List, such as MailingList or WhiteList, is reported too; the rule text gives no list of such nouns to exclude. Renaming a public property changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; FDG3068 has no code fix.

## From the book

```csharp
public class ListView {
  // good naming
  public ItemCollection Items { get; }

  // bad naming
  public ItemCollection ItemCollection { get; }
}
```
